label: original-phase token right after a u (steps 3-5), in sequences that began with t/r/o/a/k/y/l
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, almost entirely at steps 3-6 with a peak at step 4. It never fires at steps 0-2 or in the copy phase, and only weakly at <DEL>. The strongest driver is the previous input being u (20x lift, 68% of activation mass); w and v as the previous input give weaker activations. The feature also depends on which tokens came earlier: it is strongest when the prefix contains t, r, o, a, k, y or l (first_tok t has 4.6x lift, and prev2_tok r is enriched). The top examples look like t r u X or o t r u X. A prefix like x u u X does not activate it. The current input token barely matters. Activation is lower when the original sequence has more digits. The prev=u, step 3-5, seen-set predicate gets about 0.42 F1 and 0.64 mass recall on dev. The rest of the activation looks like a distributed code over the prefix contents that a simple predicate cannot fully capture.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=u (+6.26), orig1=r (+4.66), prev_tok=w (+3.92), orig0=t (+3.87), orig2=r (+3.57), orig1=t (+3.25). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-4.71), orig_idx=-1 (-4.54), orig0=u (-4.41), orig0=d (-4.38).
